name: iFlight Taurus X8 class with a RED Komodo, 6S
class: 8-inch X8 cinelifter (8 motors in coaxial pairs) carrying a cinema camera
notes: Class preset of the ready-to-fly cinelifter most often listed for Komodo-class cameras (docs/research/drones-v08.md), loaded with 2 kg of camera (a RED Komodo 6K body is 950 g; lens, media, ND and plate make up the rest), the load of iFlight's own hover-time figure. Flown by the quad model: each arm is one thrust point carrying its coaxial pair. Weights, geometry, motors, props and battery from iFlight's listing; thrust, inertia, motor lag and aerodynamics are estimates. Nothing here is endorsed by iFlight or RED.

prop_diameter_mm.note: 8 inch; the coaxial pair shares one disk

dry_mass_g.note: Taurus X8 V3 O4 6S, without battery and camera

payload_g.note: the 2 kg load of iFlight's hover-time figure (maximum payload 3 kg); a RED Komodo 6K body alone is 950 g (https://www.abelcine.com/buy/cameras-accessories/digital-cinema-cameras/red-komodo-6k-digital-cinema-camera-rf-mount-2)

battery.note: the Fullsend pack in the box

auw_g.note: take-off weight 2872 g with the 6S 5600 mAh pack + 2 kg of camera

twr.note: a 31xx of about 1100-1300KV pulls about 3.0-3.2 kg on an 8x4x3 prop at 6S alone (Scorpion MII-3011-1100: 3.2 kg); the lower prop of a coaxial pair works in the upper one's wash, a pair gives about 1.6 single props: 4 x 1.6 x 3.0 kg = 19 kg static, about 16 kg under a loaded 6S pack, / 4.87 kg = 3.3

inertia_roll_pitch_kgm2.note: sum of parts: 8 motors and props at the arm ends, arms, the 2 kg camera above and ahead of the centre, the pack

motor_tau_ms.note: J / (Kt^2/R + 2 Q0/w0) for a 3110 1250KV with an 8-inch tri-blade (about 14 g): about 50 ms, three times a 5-inch motor

motor_kappa_m.note: reaction torque / thrust of one thrust point (a coaxial pair): an 8x4 tri-blade alone is about 0.014 m (Cq/Ct about 0.07 x diameter), the lower prop needs more torque for its thrust in the upper one's wash; with it the model draws about 49 A in a hover: 5.8 min on 85 % of the pack, iFlight states 5.5 min

rpm_loaded_fraction.note: loaded rpm / (KV * V), only used for battery current

cda_horizontal_cm2.note: the camera, the pack and the frame side-on

cda_vertical_cm2.note: set so the top speed in the simulator with the camera is about 105 km/h and the full-throttle climb about 25 m/s (iFlight states 150 km/h without saying with what load); stands in for the props unloading at speed, which the model does not have

collider_duct_radius_mm.note: open props: one sphere per coaxial prop zone

collider_duct_offset_mm.note: reaches the prop tips (arm 141 mm + prop radius 102 mm)

v_crash_ms.note: a 5 kg craft with a cinema camera is done at a lower speed than a 5-inch

pack_resistance_per_cell_ohm.note: large 6S pack, wiring and XT90 included

flight_time.value: about 5.5 min hover with a 2 kg load (iFlight, 6S 5600 mAh)

camera_uptilt_deg.note: cinelifters fly slowly with the FPV camera nearly level

camera_fov_deg.note: horizontal field of view of the simulated camera

rates.note: cinelifter pilots keep their rates around 200-400 deg/s: centre 50 deg/s, 350 deg/s at full roll/pitch, 300 on yaw, expo 0.3

pid_roll.note: P, I, D, F; tuned in the simulator to a clean roll response (the Betaflight default overshoots 18-33 % on this mass and motor lag): less I and feed-forward, more D, as cinelifter pilots tune

pid_yaw.note: Betaflight default with half the feed-forward

level.note: Betaflight angle_feedforward (default 50), lowered with the PID above: at 50 this mass and 50 ms motors overshoot the 60 deg angle limit by 10 % and swing 6 deg past level when the stick is released; at 30 angle mode stops at the limit and returns to level without swinging past (sim-core test model-drones-v08, review R4)

rotor_drag_per_s.note: momentum theory sqrt(g rho A_rotors / m) = 0.57 1/s (4 disks of 8 inch, 4.87 kg) times 0.55, the open-prop share of Faessler et al. 2018

rotor_inertia_kgm2.note: two rotors per thrust point, each an 8x4 tri-blade (about 14 g, 4.8e-5 kg m^2) + a 3110 bell (about 1.1e-5)

wake_loss.note: share of thrust lost at the worst point of a descent through the rotors' own wake; a little more than a 5-inch because the lower props already fly in the upper ones' wash; sim-core wake.ts

wake_shake.note: turbulent roll/pitch torque in the wake, as a share of one thrust point's thrust times the arm (rotor thrust fluctuates by tens of per cent in the vortex-ring state)
